thesis: This episode argues that Apple is successfully expanding its ecosystem of secure, mobile-first financial services, moving from payment solutions to broader identity management and high-yield savings products. It suggests that these initiatives are designed to be financially healthy and transparent, aiming to replace insecure alternatives while fostering strong partnerships with financial institutions like Goldman Sachs.

claims.claim: Apple Pay is on a path to replace insecure wallet items with secure, private versions, allowing users to leave their wallet at home.
claims.quote: So I think all those things that you think about that you carry in your wallet or your keys, you know, we're really on a path to try to replace those with more secure and private versions of all of those. And so we know that in the future, you will be able to leave your wallet at home.

claims.claim: Apple is working with states to provision driver's licenses into Apple Wallet, with first acceptance at TSA locations.
claims.quote: We work with a number of states in the U.S. to provision state driver's licenses into your Apple Wallet. First acceptance is at TSA locations, typically in those states.

claims.claim: Apple Card was designed to be mobile first, financially healthy, and transparent, avoiding fees and offering cash back rewards.
claims.quote: So as we created Apple Card, we really wanted to do a couple things. One was make it mobile first, of course, all the way to the way we handled chat and customer service. It's all mobile first. But the other things that we really wanted to do was to make it, as I said, financially healthy. claims.claim: Apple Savings was launched when interest rates were going up, allowing Goldman to offer a high savings rate.
claims.quote: And so that was really the idea behind savings. It turns out But again, when we're talking about timing, the timing of our launch of savings was fantastic because it was when interest rates were going up. And so Goldman, our partner, was able to offer a high savings rate, which actually drove not only people to put their daily cash into their savings account, but also other deposits as well.

claims.claim: Large companies like Best Buy often have discussions about whether they should have a co-brand credit card.
claims.quote: There's always a discussion about whether Apple should have a co-brand card. Very common thing for large companies that are merchants in particular, whether you're thinking Best Buy or Macy's or whatever.
